jobDescription: A general insurer submits quarterly solvency returns to its prudential regulator and is replacing spreadsheet-based preparation with a vendor reporting platform. The Project Manager runs the change project day to day: the plan and RAID log, the steering committee packs, user acceptance testing with the finance team and the vendor's delivery milestones. The steering committee expects any benefit claimed at project closure to be measured against the baseline in the approved business case. The project sits within the finance transformation portfolio and reports each month to a steering committee chaired by the chief financial officer.
requirements: Maintains an integrated project plan and RAID log for a finance or regulatory change project.
Prepares steering committee packs and records decisions and actions.
Coordinates user acceptance testing with finance users and tracks defects to closure.
Reports realised benefits measured against the baseline in the approved business case.
Manages vendor delivery milestones against a statement of work.

evidence.text: Kept the integrated plan and RAID log for moving Marlow Mutual Insurance's quarterly solvency returns from spreadsheets to a vendor reporting platform, from mobilisation in March 2022 to closure in August 2023.
Wrote the monthly steering committee pack (status, milestones, top risks, decisions needed) and issued minutes with numbered actions after each meeting.
Coordinated three rounds of user acceptance testing with the finance reporting team, triaging 212 defects in the test management tool and chairing the daily defect call during each round.
Tracked the vendor's statement-of-work milestones, checking each deliverable against its acceptance criteria before finance released the milestone payment.
Organised the parallel run for the Q2 2023 return, reconciling the platform output against the spreadsheet output line by line with the actuarial team.

Work sample: the project closure slide pack. The milestone and defect slides match the plan. The 'Benefits' slide is a single headline, 'Manual reconciliation effort down 60%, saving £180k a year', with no table, measurement period or reference to the business case.

Reference check summary: the insurer's former finance change director confirmed in writing that the candidate was project manager for the solvency reporting project from March 2022 to August 2023 and attended every steering committee.
HR verification note: the candidate's PRINCE2 Practitioner certificate was checked on the accrediting body's successful-candidate register and is current.

propositions.text: The candidate kept the integrated plan and RAID log for the solvency returns project from March 2022 to August 2023.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the plan and RAID log, and the reference check confirms the candidate's role and dates in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate coordinated three rounds of user acceptance testing, triaging 212 defects and chairing the daily defect call.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the testing rounds and defect handling directly.

propositions.text: The solvency reporting project cut manual reconciliation effort by 60%, saving £180k a year.
propositions.rationale: The figures appear only as a headline on the candidate's closure slide, with no business-case baseline, measurement period or calculation; under the quantification rule a figure without a defined baseline is not evidence.

gold.expectedGap: No business-case baseline, measurement period or calculation supports the reconciliation-effort and cost-saving figures on the closure slide.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Report the plan and RAID log, steering packs, testing, vendor milestones and parallel run as documented; record the closure slide's effort and saving figures as an unsupported claim with a follow-up.
followUpTargets: Ask what baseline reconciliation effort the business case recorded, how effort was measured after closure, over which period, and how the annual saving was calculated.
